title: autosuggest-batch-fingerprinter: continuous workload profiling + safe-apply controller
creator: Diego Marquez
description: Build an automated batching recommendation engine that continuously profiles request workloads, synthesizes lightweight fingerprints, and proposes safe batching/caching parameter updates. The engine must produce per-model and per-route suggestions, simulate cost/latency trade-offs offline, and support a self-healing safe-apply controller that can canary, monitor, and automatically rollback changes if SLO or quality regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Engine emits per-model recommended: target_batch_size, max_batch_tokens, kv_cache_affinity, contiguous_prefix_cache_enabled, and target_continuous_batch_window_ms
Recommendations include estimated token-cost delta and expected 50/95/99 latency impact compared to baseline
Safe-apply controller can rollout to a 1% canary segment and escalate to 10% with no automated rollback for default thresholds
Automated rollback triggers if 95th latency increases >10% or token cost increases by >8% without corresponding latency benefit
Integration tests that simulate skewed workloads (burst, long-seq, short-seq) and validate rollback behavior
Dashboard shows live diff between baseline and applied config with per-token cost and success/error rates
implementation_notes: Workload fingerprint: compute per-route distributions for request length, tokens-per-request, prefix-hit-rate (KV cache), and inter-arrival histograms aggregated over 1h/24h windows
Heuristics: start with conservative rules (if median_len < 32 => small-batch profile; if prefix_hit_rate > 0.7 => enable prefix cache affinity) then refine with modeled QoS estimate
Continuous batching params: window_ms (20-200), max_batch_tokens (256-8192), min_requests_per_batch (2-8), per-model token cap to avoid OOM on large sequence models
Offline simulator: replay sampled traffic against candidate configs to estimate latency and GPU token throughput using existing runtime cost model
Safe-apply controller: stages = [plan -> canary 1% -> monitor 1h -> promote 10% -> monitor 12h -> full roll], with automated rollback hooks
Telemetry: add new metrics (batch_size_hist, applied_config_version, plan_id, prefix_cache_hit_delta) and expose to Grafana and alerts
Data retention: keep fingerprints for 90 days to support regressions and model drift analysis
rollback_plan: Automated rollback triggers: 95th latency increase >10% vs baseline OR error-rate increase >2x OR end-to-end quality regression on eval prompts >5% on canary segment
Immediate actions on rollback: revert config, mark plan as failed, notify oncall + PM + creator channel, and create postmortem ticket pre-filled with plan ID and metrics snapshot
Manual override: oncall can force rollback or pause promotion via console with single-click rollback button
Post-rollback: run synthetic replay against previous config and collect trace-level KV cache misses to inform next recommendation
